ops.title: OwnProcesses against a serving daemon's RecordPath kills its live children
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-01 by the P4.1 design re-review.

`Serve`'s singleton lock is on `socket+".lock"` (`serve.go:353-354`). `proc.OpenStore`
(`internal/proc/store.go:95`) takes **no** lock at all — its own comment says "The caller holds the
singleton flock". And `Daemon.RecordPath()` is exported (`daemon.go:41`).

So `OwnProcesses(ctx, d.RecordPath())` against a currently-serving daemon is constructible and is not
excluded: two writers on one `state.File[records]`, and worse, the CLI scope's "reclaim the prior
generation's leaked children" settles — kills — the live daemon's current children, whose generation
differs from the CLI scope's fresh one.

Not theoretical: the phase-4 consumer deltas put `Owned.Reclaimed()` and a per-agent `Serve` in the
same repo (cc-orchestrate).

Contention must return `durable.ErrLockBusy`, not root `ErrBusy` — which means "daemon already
serving" and is the wrong register.

ops.text: The record-store lock identity lives at recordPath+".lock" and is taken by both Serve and OwnProcesses
A test proves two OwnProcesses on one recordPath: the second gets durable.ErrLockBusy
A test proves OwnProcesses against a serving daemon's RecordPath() is refused rather than reclaiming its children
